note: Machine copy of lenses.md (same folder). Check ids are append-only; retire, never renumber. Read by lvr.mjs review * (contract.md, same folder).

lenses.name: Claim truth and freshness
lenses.core_question: is every factual claim true today, from a source?

checks.title: RESEARCH.md (or, scope-only, the S5 record) exists and holds sourced claims
Every price, fee, quota, limit, version, legal, regulation, market and statistic claim carries a valid cite group, a recorded answer id, or a logged `[unverified: <cat> · RQ-NNN]` marker
checks.impact_note: (I4 when a decision or cost line rests on it)
checks.signals: `cite check --all` I1 I3 I4 I9; `review claims` `source: none`

checks.title: No claim's provenance is model memory, and no recommendation leans on an unsourced "best practice"
Every cite is within its `freshness.json` limit on the review date. Expired facts are researched again now
checks.impact_note: (I4 for a price, legal or regulation fact behind an MVP cost or legal decision)

checks.title: Every load-bearing fact has evidence level 3: a primary source, or two independent fresh sources
Every load-bearing fact is fetched again in this run and compared. A changed value is a finding that names the old and new values
Where sources conflict, the conflict is recorded and resolved in the text (the freshest primary source wins), never picked silently
Every regulation claim carries a fresh amendment check
No `designer_filled` decision rests on an unverified fact. It is user-confirmed, or it is an S6 blocking risk
Every Domain Brief item has a target Section and became a question or a decision. Expired brief items are refreshed

lenses.name: Unknown-unknowns
lenses.core_question: what does the domain know that the plan does not say?

checks.title: RESEARCH.md (scope-only: the S5 record) exists
A Domain Brief exists, and each item became a question, a cited decision, or a parked note

Domain checklist. Each item is addressed with a quote, consciously parked, or na with a reason: regulation and licensing · abuse, fraud and spam · moderation of user content · offline and poor network · localization (language, currency, time zone, number format) · accessibility · store or platform policy · payments, refunds and tax · minors and age rules · data residency · support and disputes
checks.impact_note: (I4 for regulation, payments or minors when they apply)

checks.title: For the comparable products in RESEARCH.md (at least 3; research more if fewer), list what each had to handle that this plan does not mention. Sources: public docs, changelogs, policy pages, post-mortems
Write the three questions a domain expert would ask first. Each is answered in the plan (quote) or is a finding

Assumption map: every important, weakly evidenced assumption (evidence level 2 or lower) is in ASSUMPTIONS.md with how to test it, and the riskiest one is tested by an early milestone (full review only)
Inversion: list what would guarantee failure for this product type and market. The plan avoids each one (quote), or it is a finding

lenses.name: Product-type fit
lenses.core_question: does the plan meet the failure modes of its product type?

checks.title: A product type is stated somewhere in the plan
The type in state, PRD and architecture agree. A multi-type product (web + mobile) covers each type

Base pack: the release target is named (URL, store, registry or marketplace), the release proof is defined (how to show it is live or installable), the update path is defined, and the platform accounts are listed with their cost
Hosting, domain and TLS are named with their cost
Browser support and responsive layout are stated
Cookie or consent banner is decided where the market requires one
A performance budget (page weight or load time) has a check
Store accounts, fees and review guidelines are researched and cited
Every device permission has a reason shown to the user
Offline and background behaviour is defined
Minimum OS versions and device classes are stated
Store listing assets and privacy labels are planned
The core loop is defined and playable by M1
Economy and balance numbers have a tuning plan
Save, load and progress loss are handled
Age rating and platform certification are researched
A frame-rate or device performance target has a check
Rights to use the corpus are cited
The chunking and embedding choice has a reason
An evaluation set with expected answers and a pass threshold exists
A hallucination guard exists: answers cite their source, and the system refuses when no source is found
Re-indexing and its cost are planned
Tool schemas validate their input
The auth and transport choice (stdio or HTTP) has a reason
Rate limits and timeouts are set
Prompt injection through tool output and other untrusted content is handled
It is tested against at least one named client
Where credentials are stored is decided
Retries and idempotency are defined (a re-run does not double-send)
Execution quota and plan limits are cited
An error branch with an alert exists
The trigger choice (webhook or polling) has a reason
The trigger description says when the skill fires and when it does not
A harness compatibility list exists
Install, update and uninstall paths are defined
Tool and permission scope is minimal
Install channels and supported OSes are stated
The flags, exit codes and stdout/stderr contract is defined
Config and secrets locations are defined
Help text and error messages are planned
The manifest version is stated and permissions are minimal
The store review policy is researched
Host permissions and content-script injection risks are handled
Cross-browser support is stated
System prompt guardrails and refusal rules are defined
Destructive tools need confirmation
An eval set with red-team prompts exists
Cost per conversation and context limits are modeled
A path to a human or a fallback exists

lenses.name: Scope and MVP discipline
lenses.core_question: is the MVP the smallest thing that proves the idea, and is scope locked and traceable?

checks.title: SCOPE.md (scope-only: the proposal) exists
Every S4 feature, and every S4-additions capture, is classified in-MVP or Parking Lot exactly once. Full review: scope is locked (conventions §5)
Each in-MVP feature names its user job (who, and what for) and a kill criterion (what result would drop it)

Traceability. Every in-MVP F-NN has a requirements block, a USER_FLOWS section, a SCOPE row and exactly one milestone. Every parked F-NN has a requirements row marked parked, a USER_FLOWS heading marked parked, and a scope row with a reason
checks.impact_note: (I4 when a feature has no milestone)
checks.signals: crosscheck X1; lint B5 B9 F1–F4

checks.title: No orphans: no requirement without a feature, and no milestone without a covered feature (parked features need no milestone)
Smallest proof: an in-MVP feature that the core value does not need is a finding (its fix is a decision: park it)
Hidden creep: a non-functional line (admin panel, analytics, multi-language, export) that adds work without an F-id or a milestone
Parking Lot rows are intact: none deleted, renumbered or quietly moved into the MVP

lenses.name: Builder dry-run (buildability)
lenses.core_question: can a builder agent run M0 from the bundle alone, without guessing?

checks.title: AGENTS.md and MILESTONES.md exist
All 20 bundle entries exist and are non-empty
AGENTS.md states what the product is, the load order (DECISIONS → SPEC → MILESTONES → VERIFICATION), the working rules, and a file map. It needs no LVR skill
Local run is complete: prerequisites with versions, install steps, env vars with placeholder values (no real secrets), the run command, and the expected output
No bundle file requires reading `.lvr/` (appending open questions to the journal is the only allowed use)
Every relative file pointer resolves
CODE_STYLE.md and SECURITY.md are specific to the chosen stack, not generic filler

Dry-run of M0, then M1: walk each deliverable and acceptance step as a builder who holds only the bundle files. Every point where a decision, value, command, path, credential, version or expected result is missing is one finding, located at that step

No vague words in anything the builder must follow: "appropriate", "etc.", "similar", "as needed", "TBD", "TODO", "should probably", "some". Each one inside a requirement, step or acceptance criterion is a finding
Every in-MVP feature can be built with the recorded stack, accounts, devices and budget. Nothing needs an account, service or device that the S2 record lacks
CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are exactly the one-line pointer. When handoff is done, HANDOFF-PROMPT.md exists and holds the full builder rule set

lenses.name: Data and state
lenses.core_question: is every entity, owner, lifecycle, migration, retention, backup and PII path defined?

checks.title: SPEC/data-model.md exists
Every entity the requirements touch is in the data model with fields, keys and relations, and no model entity is unused
Each entity has a create, read, update and delete owner (which feature, which role)
Lifecycle: retention, deletion (including deletion on user request), and what happens to existing data on a schema change. There must be a migration story, never "delete the database"
checks.impact_note: (I4 when real user data is lost)

checks.title: Concurrency and duplicates: two writes at once, a double submit, and retries are handled with idempotency keys or unique constraints
Backup and restore: where, how often, and how a restore is tested
Every personal field is in the SECURITY.md PII inventory with its protection
Import, export and data portability are planned, or a decision says they are not needed

lenses.name: Security, privacy, legal and ToS
lenses.core_question: what is the worst thing an attacker, a user or a regulator can do?

checks.title: SECURITY.md exists
Authentication and authorization per route, tool or screen: who may do what, with admin paths named
Secrets: where each one lives and who rotates it. Never in the repo; the example env file has placeholders only
Privacy: the PII inventory matches the data model. A privacy-policy decision exists whenever there is a login, PII or a store presence. Consent is planned where the region requires it
Region rules for the confirmed market (data residency, consumer, age and sector rules) are cited and fresh
The legal and ToS position of every integration, scraping or automation flow is cited, and either resolved or accepted as a `user_confirmed` decision with the cost written
Dependency licenses fit the product (no NC or copyleft surprise in a closed product), and NC items are runtime-only
Untrusted input is handled: injection (SQL, prompt, HTML), uploads, rate limits and abuse controls on public endpoints
Payments: the product stores no card data unless the plan covers the required compliance, and refunds and chargebacks are handled

lenses.name: Cost and capacity
lenses.core_question: do money and quota hold at 10× and at 0.1× usage, and who pays when they don't?

checks.title: A cost table exists
A per-unit cost model exists for every usage-priced item (LLM tokens, API calls, messages, storage, egress, seats): unit, price and assumed volume
At 10× the stated volume, the monthly cost, every free-tier cliff and every quota are computed, and the plan says who pays and what breaks
checks.impact_note: (I4 when the ceiling breaks with no cap)

checks.title: At 0.1× the volume, fixed costs (minimum plans, annual commitments) still fit the budget
The recurring total fits the S2 budget ceiling, and every one-time cost is shown
Every usage-based cost has a cap or an alert (a spending limit or a quota alarm). No bill is unbounded
Totals agree: the `blueprint.json` costs, the RESEARCH.md table and the OVERVIEW.md totals
One realistic bad month (traffic spike, abuse, a retry loop) is priced with the uplift rules (scale.md U2, U3)

lenses.name: Schedule and milestone sizing
lenses.core_question: are milestones small and honestly sized, with an outside view?

checks.title: MILESTONES.md exists
M0 is a walking skeleton: the real stack, the real data store, one real user task end to end, and one scripted check
Each milestone fits one focused builder session, and no milestone bundles unrelated features
Each estimate names a reference class (or says "none: novel") and shows the uplift-adjusted figure (scale.md U1)
The order follows dependencies, the critical path is visible, and the riskiest assumption is tested early (L02.5)
A failure is budgeted for every integration step that assumes it "works first try" (U4)
External waits are scheduled: store review, domain and DNS, API key approval, legal review

lenses.name: Dependencies, integrations and one-way doors
lenses.core_question: what external thing can break us, and what can't be undone?

checks.title: SPEC/architecture.md (scope-only: the S5 record) exists
Every external dependency has a license, an install line, a pinned version and a fallback for when it is unavailable
Versions are current, and no dependency reaches end of life within a year (cited)
The rate limits and quotas of each integration are cited at the lowest tier the plan uses (U5)
The cost of moving away from each core vendor is written

One-way doors: each irreversible step (domain, store listing, production data schema, public API, pricing promise, vendor contract, messages sent to users) has its undo cost and who holds the handle, traced rather than asserted
Every account, key and approval the build needs is listed with its owner and lead time

lenses.name: Internal coherence
lenses.core_question: do all files say the same thing?

checks.title: DECISIONS.md exists
Every `decisions[]` entry has an id, a section, a summary, a non-empty rationale and a valid status
DECISIONS.md mirrors `decisions[]`: the same ids and statuses, nothing extra
ASSUMPTIONS.md lists every assumed and `designer_filled` decision with why and how to confirm it, and each one is still valid
No two decisions contradict each other, and no decision contradicts the locked scope
The display name, feature names, stack and entity names are identical across files
Counts and numbers agree across files (feature count, milestone count, prices, limits)
Every file is English GFM with ASCII diagrams only: no Mermaid and no unfilled placeholders
OVERVIEW.md Limitations lists every degraded booster (by tier), every failed delegation and every blocked-then-resolved Section
`blueprint.json` matches state and bundle
State is consistent: `state.json` is valid, Section statuses match their records, milestone ids, goals and order match MILESTONES.md, `project.status` matches progress, and the journal is healthy
Every accepted S6 risk points at a `user_confirmed` decision with the accepted cost written

lenses.name: Verification and testability
lenses.core_question: can "done" be proved by a command?

checks.title: VERIFICATION.md exists
Every acceptance criterion has a procedure with exact commands and expected outputs (or an observable visual fact and how to look)
Every critical path has at least one negative test (wrong password, empty cart, quota hit)
Test data: where it comes from and how to reset it
Every external integration has a check that fails loudly when it silently breaks
The global smoke test is one real end-to-end pass, and "definition of verified" is stated
Every check can be run by the builder alone, with no judgement words such as "looks good"

lenses.name: Operability and failure modes (FMEA)
lenses.core_question: what fails in production, and who notices?

checks.title: SPEC/architecture.md and HANDOVER.md exist
FMEA table: each component × failure mode has severity, occurrence and detection, plus a mitigation or a verification step. Every failure point named in the architecture has one
Backup and restore are tested, not only described
Monitoring and alerting say who notices an outage, and how fast
Rollback: how to undo a bad deploy
Rotation and expiry of secrets, certificates, API keys and tokens are planned
HANDOVER.md covers run, deploy, update, backup, where secrets live, and who to ask
Single points of failure (one server, one maintainer, one key holder) are named with their recovery

lenses.name: UX and flow completeness
lenses.core_question: does every path a real user takes exist in the spec?

checks.title: USER_FLOWS.md exists
Every in-MVP F-id has a flow with a numbered script, and every flow maps to an F-id
Each screen or command in the flows has its empty, loading, error, offline and success states
First run and onboarding, permission denied and session expired are covered
Destructive actions ask for confirmation, and can be undone where possible
Basic accessibility (contrast, keyboard, screen reader) and the market's language, currency and date formats are covered
Each flow's failure path ends where the user can act

lenses.name: Second- and third-order effects and adoption

checks.title: SPEC/prd.md (scope-only: the S1 record) exists
The success metric is defined and measurable, and the plan says how it will be measured
Every pre-mortem cause (protocol P2) is mapped. This lens owns the unmapped ones
Who maintains it after launch is named, with time per week and cost
Behaviour change: how users could game, abuse or work around it, and what happens at success (load, support, moderation)
Platform dependency: what happens when the main platform changes its terms, price or API
Adoption: how the first users find it and start using it, and what stops them
